component.name: Charlie
component.summary: A focused email client without all of the nonsense

description.p: Charlie is Luma's native adaptive mail client. It keeps accounts together, groups replies into readable conversations, and preserves the same actions from wide desktop windows to handheld presentation.
Google OAuth is unavailable in this release. Existing mail and saved sign-in grants remain preserved. Gmail app passwords and supported Microsoft sign-in remain available.
Independent interface updates preserve the existing mailbox. A native mail service owns credentials and account authentication.
Introduced provider-first Luma account setup for Google, Microsoft, iCloud, Yahoo, Fastmail, Zoho, AOL and standards-based IMAP.
Retires stale sign-in notifications after a proven account login.
Recovered stale Gmail access tokens, added cached account and sender avatars, and opened complete formatted messages from their email surface.
Expanded complete formatted messages inline with one compact collapse control.
Improved formatted-mail expansion with a deeper fade and full-width collapse footer.
Expanded formatted messages in place with a centered text affordance and readable lower fade.
Displayed message times and relative dates in the system's local timezone.
Charlie checks mail in the background while its window is closed and shows who wrote and what about, with private text on the lock screen.
Searching mail from the desktop no longer opens Charlie at sign-in.
Stopped reporting transient IMAP connection failures as rejected credentials.
Kept Charlie running by minimizing its main window when the close control is used.
Corrected the installed icon to use Luma's rounded platform silhouette.
Simplified conversational HTML, quoted history, embedded images and mirrored sent metadata.
Polished message conversations, formatted mail, attachment actions and Sent-folder threading.
Added account management, Google browser authentication and Gmail XOAUTH2.
Polished adaptive pane measures, thread alignment and compact navigation.
Initial Luma-native development candidate.
